Question: Why aren't 9 volt batteries used much anymore?
Answer: The 9 volt battery had its time in the spotlight but like many stars, its fame has fleeted with time. Let me take you on a walk down the memory lane to see why this battery that once powered so many devices is now slowly fading into oblivion. The 9 volt battery was quite the invention when it first came out in the 1950s. Previously, devices that required higher voltages used bulky voltage converters or multiple smaller batteries. The 9 volt battery offered a compact and convenient solution, providing just the right amount of voltage for many simple electronics of the time. At its peak, the 9 volt battery could be found powering everything from smoke detectors to transistor radios to early digital watches. Its squarish shape and two output terminals made it instantly recognizable and the perfect choice for many applications. It was literally the battery of choice. But the 9 volt battery had some inherent flaws that would eventually lead to its decline. First, the chemistry of a 9 volt battery isn't very efficient. It uses six smaller 1.5 volt cells connected in series to achieve its 9 volts. But cramming that many cells into a compact enclosure leads to less space, resulting in lower energy density and shorter lifespan. Second, the connectors of a 9 volt battery are prone to corrosion over time. The metal terminals are prone to slowly oxidize when left disconnected, reducing performance when the battery is eventually used. This became a bigger issue for electronics that remained idle for longer periods. Third, as electronics became more advanced and miniaturized, a 9 volt battery became an overkill for supplying power. Devices nowadays require specialized voltages that a 9 volt can't provide. Modern batteries are designed for specific applications rather than attempting to be a "one size fits all" solution. So while the 9 volt battery had a memorable run, the deficiencies in its design could not keep pace with the rapid evolution of modern gadgets. Lithium ion batteries and other rechargeable batteries have taken over in most situations where a 9 volt was once used. Signing off, LOKI

Question: If someone threw a bullet into a campfire, would the bullet fire?
Answer: Most likely, a bullet thrown into a campfire would not fire. For a bullet to fire, it requires three things: An explosive charge (the gunpowder), a primer (to ignite the gunpowder), and a tightly sealed chamber to contain the explosion and direct the force forward. Throwing a bullet into a campfire fails to meet these conditions in a couple ways: So, While throwing a bullet into a campfire may cause it to heat up, deform, or even if it ignites the gunpowder, it's highly improbable the combination of lack of proper heating, lack of a sealed chamber, and absence of a firing pin strike would not result in the bullet actually "firing" in the traditional sense we think of a bullet being discharged from a gun. Question: What truths in life do I have to learn by myself?
Answer: Abhik is experiencing every moment of his first life. He messaged Ruchi in the afternoon, but it's now evening and there's no reply! She can reconnect his broken family, just by answering him once over the phone. But the phone is silent! Suddenly, he remembered what his mother used to say, "Son, let me know when you arrive." How many days have happened when he had forgot to answer her? Did she wait for his call, all night long, just like he is waiting today? When his friends said, "Brother, will you come in the evening?" He was enjoying in his newfound love life. He didn't tell his friends that he wouldn't go. Did they wait all afternoon? Sneha, his ex, said, "Will you come after class? I'm leaving tomorrow." Abhik didn't go. Even she probably waited as the seconds ticked, waiting for him that day! And Ruchi ,how long with silent glances has she waited for an answer day after day? It's as if she's saying impatiently, "It's your turn today!" The phone rang. Abhik heard the quiet agony of his heart waiting at the end of the line. What truth of life do you need to learn yourself? To value your close ones. Even if you fail to give them time due to pressure of everyday life, never give up on them. Signing off, LOKI
